trust_decision.summary: Which request-body charset the standalone server's JSON body parser will decode for an untrusted client; at the pinned commit any charset declared in Content-Type is decoded, and the fix adds a UTF-8/16/32 allowlist in a body-parser verify hook (415 otherwise).

landing_point.why: The advisory title names startStandaloneServer; its only body-parsing call is express.json({ limit: '50mb' }) on this line.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API startStandaloneServer() from @apollo/server/standalone -> HTTP POST to any path

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other body-reaching route, expressMiddleware, does no body parsing and requires the user's own json middleware (packages/server/src/express4/index.ts:47-57); the changeset says non-standalone users were not affected, so it is legitimately out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests with no charset, or charset=utf-8 / UTF-8 / utf-16(le|be) (the latter non-functional upstream on 4.x for utf-32), plus whitespace/parameters around application/json, must keep being accepted; an over-broad fix that rejects any charset parameter or non-exact Content-Type breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: utf-32 / utf-32le / utf-32be (allowed by the regex)
exotic single/multibyte charsets (win1251, iso-8859-1, windows936) rejected

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second body parser (e.g. express.text for application/graphql or express.urlencoded) mounted next to express.json in the standalone app, decoding the declared charset the same way
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Many GraphQL servers accept application/graphql bodies; a maintainer adding that convenience would reuse body-parser defaults, which decode any iconv charset.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fallback in expressMiddleware that parses req.body itself when no json middleware ran, instead of returning 500
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at that spot already anticipates users forgetting body-parser; an auto-parse fallback is a plausible convenience, and it would be a second implementation in another module.

O9_family: resource exhaustion via attacker-chosen request-body charset decoding (filed as CWE-1333; mechanism is costly charset decoding, not a project regex)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm workspaces, tsc, jest 29 (4.x branch, express 4)
O10_build.project_tests: packages/server/src/__tests__/standalone/standaloneSpecific.test.ts (Configuration block, incl. >100KiB body test at :109); the fix adds the 'Request body charset handling' describe block and needs devDeps iconv-lite and content-type

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Lower the 50mb limit or reject any Content-Type with a charset parameter, instead of allowlisting UTF-8/16/32 charsets.

out_of_scope_notes: The pinned tree is the 4.x line (express4, standalone built on express); fix commit d25a5bdc targets the 5.x layout (bodyParser + http.createServer) and does not apply here; e9d49d16 is the matching 4.x fix.
The docs example at docs/source/api/standalone.mdx (swapping to expressMiddleware) uses express.json without a charset check; it is docs only, and the 5.x fix updates it.
unverified: Whether content-type and iconv-lite are installed in node_modules at the pinned tree (content-type is normally a transitive dep of express/body-parser) was not checked.
Exact cost profile of body-parser/iconv decoding of exotic charsets was not examined (out of scope: no running).
